text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unknown gunmen fire at opposition NADECO vice-chairman Abraham Adesanya in his car in Lagos but he escapes unhurt.
- The all-military Provisional Ruling Council approves the 1997 fiscal budget after two days of deliberations but does not say when it will be announced.

- Federal Appeal Court in capital Abuja to rule next Tuesday on whether detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola should be brought to court to name which of two rival lawyers will represent him in his treason trial.
- Joint venture of state oil firm NNPC and Shell budget 54 billion naira for six new projects aimed at cutting gas flaring.
- Nigerian Postal Services introduces quarterly rental payments for post office boxes to reduce debts by subscribers.
- Oil marketing firm Texaco Nigeria appoints first African chief executive officer to succeed American Tom Hauck who is being transferred to the United States.

- Conglomerate United Africa Company of Nigeria acquires 60 percent stake in Grand Cereals and Oil Mills Ltd, located in Bukim, central Nigeria, to enhance its investments in the food and beverage business.

- Any of the five registered political parties that receives less than 10 percent of total votes cast in any national election will be banned, says Sam Grace Ikoku, deputy chairman of the Transitional Implementation Programme.
- State-owned Nigerian Agricultural and Cooperative Bank may collapse if government fails to provide funds for its operations, according to its chief executive officer Isa Tahir.
- Federal government and six multinational oil firms which are in joint venture operations in Nigerian oil industry are yet to resolve the issue of profit margins, sources say.
